title: canary-fallback-playbook-arch-review-notes
agenda: Review RFC: Canary + multi-tier fallback policy (draft)
Decide canonical fallback chain for hosted vs dedicated
Monitoring and alert thresholds for canary failures
Rollout / rollback playbook and Console surface requirements
content:
Summary:

This meeting captured the architecture review for the Canary + Multi-tier Fallback playbook intended to make model rollouts and runtime degradations predictable across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The draft RFC (linked) proposes an ordered fallback chain that preserves functionality where possible while minimizing latency and cost spikes.

Key decisions made (consensus):

1) Canonical fallback chain (ordered) - agreed for general use across Hosted and Dedicated, with minor config differences for Private: 
   - primary: continue to attempt primary model & node pool (short retries at routing layer)
   - fallback-1: route to quantized/4-bit-compatible variant of same model (if available)
   - fallback-2: route to smaller-capacity variant (e.g., medium instead of large) keeping same tokenizer/header
   - fallback-3: route to regional replica or lower-cost region within latency threshold
   - fallback-4: degrade generation configuration (reduce max_tokens, increase temperature determinism, enable early stopping)
   - fallback-5: graceful feature degradation (disable streaming/chunks, return summarized output)
   - last-resort: return 503 + Retry-After and increment per-route incident counter

Rationale: The chain prefers behavioral-preserving options first (quantized variant -> smaller size) before degrading user-visible behavior. Routing to a regional replica is preferred over changing output quality unless regional latency would break SLOs. Returning 503 is treated as a controlled failure only after all other mitigations fail.

2) Canary policy for model rollouts
   - Canary size: default 5% traffic for 24 hours with automatic extension checks tied to quality and infra metrics.
   - Stop conditions (immediate rollback): error rate spike > 3x baseline OR p95 latency > SLO + 200ms sustained 5m OR token-cost-per-request > 2x expected for 10m window.
   - Soft-fail conditions (halt promotion): sustained p95 > SLO + 100ms OR generation-quality regression on golden prompts (see Eval harness) > configurable threshold.

3) Metadata and model catalog changes
   - Require model variants to expose metadata flags: quantized_compatible (bool), quality_tier (high/medium/low), latency_estimate_ms (for seq=64/256), fallback_priority (int).
   - Console should surface these fields in rollout UI and allow manual override of fallback order per deployment.

4) Observability & alerting
   - Add per-route metrics: fallback_activation_count, fallback_level_histogram, token_cost_delta, canary_p95, canary_error_rate.
   - Alerts: canary_error_rate > threshold, fallback_activation_count spike (>20x baseline in 5m), fallback_level_histogram skew to >2 (meaning deep fallbacks engaged). Integrate alerts into SRE pager rotations for Dedicated customers with SLAs.

5) API / runtime changes
   - Routing policy proto extension to accept fallback chain (list of model variant ids + triggers).
   - Implement non-blocking routing path evaluation with time budget (e.g., 30ms) to avoid adding latency during decision making.

Design options discussed (and tradeoffs):

A) Push logic into control plane vs keep routing decisions in runtime
   - Control plane approach (pro): easier to reason and debug, simpler policy changes; (con): higher control plane load, edge decisions slower during incidents.
   - Runtime approach (pro): faster failover, local decisions on node; (con): harder to propagate global metrics, more coupling to runtime code.
   - Decision: hybrid. Control plane publishes canonical fallback chains and thresholds. Runtime evaluates local viability and executes fast routing decisions using cached metadata and a short evaluation budget.

B) Quantized variant first vs smaller size first
   - Quantized-first preserves logits/semantics but may have variable latency depending on kernel support. Smaller-size-first preserves kernel path but can change semantics.
   - Decision: quantized-first when quantized_compatible = true and latency_estimate within SLO margin. Otherwise prefer smaller-size variant.

C) Canary duration & size
   - Options considered: short (1h) many canaries vs long (24h) single canary.
   - Decision: default 24h 5% with ability to configure per-customer. Shorter rolling experiments supported by engineering for rapid iterations.

- Spec updates (this doc -> RFC v1.1) — owner: Priya — due 2025-10-03 (IN PROGRESS)
- Model catalog metadata proto + DB migration — owner: Jun Park — due 2025-10-17

- Console UI for fallback config & canary controls — owner: Maya Li — due 2025-11-07
- Observability: metrics + dashboards + alert rules — owner: Lena Ortiz (SRE) — due 2025-10-24
- Integration tests + canary harness (end-to-end) — owner: Omar Bennett — due 2025-11-14
- Customer-facing docs & runbook — owner: Tom Wu (Solutions) — due 2025-11-21

Action items (explicit):

1) Jun: draft model metadata migration plan and backward compatibility story; include fallback_priority mapping — due 2025-10-10.
2) Elias: prototype runtime evaluation with 30ms decision budget; demo to team — due 2025-10-20.
3) Maya: mockups for Console rollout control showing fallback chain visualization and manual override — due 2025-10-13.
4) Lena: propose SLO-based alert thresholds and playbook to route pages to SRE vs customer success — due 2025-10-15.
5) Omar: create E2E test matrix (hosted + dedicated) and add golden prompt suite for canary checks — due 2025-10-18.
6) Priya: update RFC and coordinate with Product for default canary policy — due 2025-10-03.

Open questions / risks (to be resolved):

- Private deployments: customers may want to fully control fallback order. We need to define which fields are editable on Private vs Hosted. (Action: Priya to propose policy matrix by 2025-10-06.)
- Cost signal sensitivity: fallback chains that route to larger regional capacity could increase spend; need cost-budget guardrails. (Action: Product/Finance sync. JIRA ENG-4182 assigned.)
- Model semantic drift: switching to smaller variants or quantized models can change outputs. Need tighter eval harness and possibly a rollback automation based on golden prompt regressions. (Action: Omar + Research to propose regression thresholds by 2025-10-14.)

Backward compatibility notes:

- Runtimes must continue to respect existing model aliasing; new fallback_priority and quantized_compatible fields should default to safe values (fallback_priority=100, quantized_compatible=false) so there is no behavioral change for models without metadata. Migration plan will include a phased agent update and feature flag gate.

Post-meeting next steps:

- Priya to publish RFC v1.1 with decisions and updated action items to Confluence (link in metadata) and ping architects for formal sign-off.
- Schedule deep-dive on runtime evaluation prototype with SRE and infra teams (30m) week of 2025-10-20.
- Start catalog metadata migration planning ASAP to unlock automated fallback chains.

Notes for reviewers:

- Focus review on: fallback ordering rationale, canary stop/hard-fail conditions, and what fields must be configurable per-customer vs global.
- If you rely on on-prem customers, call out specific constraints in comments on the Confluence RFC (see linked artifacts).
